_comment: Canonical axis-aligned box semantics. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'what a box is' and the geometry questions asked of it (area, center, overlap, normalization). Before this contract, composition_planner and compiler/negative_space each carried their own helpers, with two different box shapes (dict vs tuple) and a divergent area rule.
box: (x, y, w, h) in pixels; x,y is the top-left corner
normalized_box: (nx, ny, nw, nh) in 0..1; pixels = (nx*W, ny*H, nw*W, nh*H)
area: max(0, w) * max(0, h)  -- degenerate boxes contribute zero, never negative
overlap: positive intersection area strictly greater than a tolerance (default 2px on each axis)

known_divergences._comment: Tracked, not hidden. Quantified by runtime/geometry/audit.py.
known_divergences.composition_planner._area: unclamped w*h -> differs from canonical only for degenerate (negative-dimension) boxes
